purpose: Quarantine a literature-derived disclosure-timing mechanism for source/PIT feasibility before any formal performance path.

external_basis.source: Flugum, Bergsma Lovelace & Wang (2026), Does the Market Information Processing Context Matter? How Past Disclosure Timing Affects Future Stock Returns
external_basis.observation: The working paper proposes an information-processing-frictions measure based on a firm's tendency to file 8-Ks in challenging market information-processing environments and studies subsequent cross-sectional returns.

candidates.name: Filing Timing × Information-Processing Friction
candidates.hypothesis: The market response to a newly public issuer disclosure may depend on whether that disclosure arrives during a high-information-processing-load market context, creating a timing-context state distinct from filing volume alone.
candidates.construction: Combine the frozen SEC filing-arrival state with a separately deterministic public market information-processing-context state. The project adaptation must use only variables whose public availability is independently timestamped and must freeze the exact context construction before any performance evaluation.
candidates.next_gate: source/PIT feasibility plus deterministic processing-context contract and mutation tests
literature_basis: Does the Market Information Processing Context Matter? How Past Disclosure Timing Affects Future Stock Returns (2026)

notes: This is a discovery hypothesis, not project evidence.
The cited working paper is source inspiration only; its reported empirical findings are not project evidence.
The project must not copy the source result into a candidate score or gate.
No candidate is ranked, selected, tuned or performance-authorized.
The first technical question is whether a deterministic, free/public processing-context variable can be reconstructed without hindsight.
